response: {"text":"The paper looks at how the classic verses of an indigenous Central Mexican language are put together and how they differ across various manuscript groups. By comparing several versions that appear in old songbooks and narrative collections, the study shows how later scribes and readers altered the verses over time. It argues that these differences are key to grasping the way the poems were passed down orally and how their internal patterns are organized. The author also suggests a step‑by‑step approach for rebuilding the earliest form of a poem, which helps both translation and deeper analysis. The findings point out that, while certain parts of the verses stay the same, other sections vary, shedding light on the structural rules and cultural identity embedded in this indigenous poetic tradition."}
